Hi Alice —

Great to connect today. As promised, a concise recap of the POC scope and the proposed integration plan so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and owners.

Summary of goals (what ACME wants to validate)
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 300ms for <512-token prompts under expected qps.
- Quality: >85% acceptance rate on representative prompt set (we'll run evaluation harness).
- Cost: token-unit cost target within the threshold you shared (we'll track during the trial).
- Feature tests: streaming/partial responses and tool-calling for retrieval integration must work end-to-end.

Proposed evaluation plan
1) Week 0 (kickoff): access, onboarding, and SDK walk-through.
2) Week 1: integration + smoke tests (streaming, tool calling, auth).
3) Week 2: run production-like evals on your prompt set; gather latency/cost metrics.
4) Week 3: iterate on batching/quantization and confirm success criteria.

Timeline & ownership
- Kickoff meeting: propose Tue Oct 7, preferred morning PT — will set calendar once you confirm.
- Redwood owners: Marissa Cole (AM), Dev Patel (Solutions Engineer) — technical lead.
- ACME owners: Alice Chen (product), Bob Li (engineering) — please confirm.

Integration notes (high level)
- SDKs: We support JS/Python/Go — for streaming we recommend the SDK streaming client (SSE/websocket-backed).
- API routes: use /v1/generate for standard generation, /v1/stream for streaming responses; tool calling via /v1/call or via function-calling payloads in the SDK.
- Auth: API keys with scoped roles for the POC; will provide a short-lived key in the kickoff.
- Attachments: draft integration guide + mutual action plan attached.

Open questions for you
- Can Bob be the technical owner for the POC?
- Do you have a sandbox environment we should target for initial tests, or should we use Redwood test tenant?

Next steps
- Please confirm owners and the kickoff slot (Oct 7 morning PT).
- I'll share the integration guide and a small sample repo before kickoff.

Thanks — talk soon.

Alice / Bob — quick follow-up with the integration guide attached and a few concrete implementation notes below. Attaching redwood_integration_guide_v1.pdf and the mutual action plan (xlsx).

Streaming support
- Yes: we support token-streaming via SSE/WebSocket. The SDK exposes a .stream() client that yields token chunks as they arrive. Example JS (pseudo):

  const client = new RedwoodSDK({ apiKey: process.env.RDW_KEY });
  const stream = client.stream({ route: '/v1/stream', model: 'redwood-xxl' });
  for await (const chunk of stream) { renderChunk(chunk.text); }

Tool calling / function hooks
- Redwood supports declarative tool schemas registered in the model call. The SDK will surface a function-calling API: pass a list of tools (name + JSON schema) and the model can return a call request which the SDK will surface to your code to execute. We can also proxy tool calls to your internal endpoints if you prefer.

API routes (short)
- POST /v1/generate — standard synchronous generation.
- POST /v1/stream — streaming responses (SSE).
- POST /v1/call — function/tool execution handshake (optional; SDK abstracts most flows).

Auth & scopes
- For the POC we will issue a scoped API key limited to the sandbox tenant and the test models. Keys are time-limited and auditable.

Recommended defaults for the POC
- Concurrency: start with 5 concurrent streams per container and adjust based on latency during week 1.
- Batching: enable automatic micro-batching (default) — we can toggle during tests.
- KV cache: enable prefix KV caching for repeated context to reduce token usage.

Attachments:
- redwood_integration_guide_v1.pdf (attached) — includes sample code, SDK links, and troubleshooting.
- poc_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (attached) — owner-level tasks and dates.

I'll let Dev chime in with exact curl/SDK snippets and a repo link. If those look good, I'll schedule the Oct 7 kickoff for 10:00 AM PT.

Hi Bob / Alice — Dev from Redwood here (solutions eng). A few technical details and a sample repo to speed up onboarding.

Auth & environment
- We'll create a sandbox-scoped API key for your sandbox.acme.internal tenant. Key will be valid for 21 days by default.
- If you prefer IP allowlisting, tell us the CIDR ranges for the sandbox.

Sample curl (sync)
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $RDW_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-xxl","input":"Summarize this..."}'

Sample JS SDK snippet (streaming)
  import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RDW_KEY });
  const stream = client.stream({ model: 'redwood-xxl', input: 'Draft an email' });
  stream.on('token', (t) => process.stdout.write(t));
  stream.on('done', () => console.log('stream finished'));

Rate limits and concurrency
- For the POC we recommend: 100 req/min initial limit, 10 concurrent streams per account. We can increase if you need more.

Tool calling details
- Define tools as JSON schema objects; the SDK validates model outputs and surfaces a tool call event to your handler. We can also configure webhooks so the tool call executes server-side in Redwood and returns the result.

Repo + samples
- Repo: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-samples (sample app, cURL examples, postman collection).

Next steps I can take this week
- Provision sandbox API key and attach to the mutual action plan.
- Spin up a short test harness that exercises streaming + tool calling against your sandbox.

I'll plan for the Oct 7 kickoff at 10:00 AM PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in and an agenda.

Thanks — looking forward.
